assessment: The incumbent can work with little handling: unchanged-assignment files had a seven-minute median. Overall, however, only 32/40 contained the intended course set and median handling was 17 minutes. Current-assignment semantics plausibly contribute to transition-week errors, but association is not causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Execution takes seconds while replacements take much longer; this does not establish that waiting accounts for measured handling time. No cross-center rows were observed, but the omitted split-course center limits that evidence. Neither the source of intended-course truth nor spreadsheet effort is established.

openings.claim: Requested-week course membership and stable course identity may diverge from current assignments or displayed names, causing some apparent omissions.
openings.delta: Distinguishes actual row exclusion from renamed courses that are present but unrecognized; reassignment alone cannot explain all affected files.
openings.prediction: If selection uses inappropriate current state, identical weekly attendance will produce different course coverage after a reassignment. If names cause recognition failures, stable course IDs will show coverage despite a reported omission.
openings.probe: In private staging, run fabricated unchanged, midweek-reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures against an explicitly agreed weekly course set. Compare internal IDs and CSV rows, test a second center for leakage, and exercise attendance entry during export. Retain the documented CSV schema.
assumptions: Fixtures can define intended membership unambiguously.
These are diagnostic runs; historical-state availability and repair effort remain unknown.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from reconciling competing course lists, or from downloading and spreadsheet import?
openings.delta: Separates coordinator effort from replacement elapsed time and locates the next bounded intervention.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation-dominated account predicts more active checking and correction for transition cases; an import-dominated account predicts similar import effort across stable and transition cases.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated stable and transition files, counterbalancing order. Time checking, correction, download and import separately; record replacement waiting separately and each coordinator's intended course set before inspection.
assumptions: Cap combined diagnostic work within six engineer-days and existing hosting; findings alone do not establish the next-40-export target.
